content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to challenge Whoop. The company is reportedly "developing prototypes," but has not yet decided whether to ultimately bring the product to market.

The prototype developed internally at Apple reportedly features "a thin fabric strap with a built-in sensor computer module." The project is currently in the "technical exploration" phase, and Bloomberg reports the product will not launch before 2028, provided Apple ultimately decides to release it.

The project is said to have the support of senior Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took over the leadership of Apple's health team after Jeff Williams departed last October.

Products like Whoop and the Oura Ring are popular among users who don't want to wear a smartwatch but still want to track their health and fitness. According to Reuters, Oura is gearing up for an IPO and recently disclosed that it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ending June 30. Revenue grew 74% to $1.21 billion in the nine months ending June 30.

However, Apple remains the dominant player in the smartwatch market. Apple Watch offers significantly more features than health- and fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.
